# 2.1.0: the folders that merge into their slice, enumerated

Release 2.1.0 stops deriving the slice from the shape of a path and asks the filesystem
instead. Between the layer and the first configured segment the plugin walks the folders of
the path and settles on the deepest one that holds a public api file.

One consequence of that change removes reports, so the design it came from requires the
removals to be enumerated somewhere durable rather than summarised. This file is that
enumeration. The release notes in `2.1.0.md` describe the shape and the calibration; the
per project membership lives here.

## What a merged group is

A merged group is a folder the resolver settles on for two or more of the slice names the
old path heuristic derived. Every name in the group except one is a folder inside the slice
rather than a slice of its own, so an import between two of them stops being a cross slice
import and its report disappears.

Exactly one member of every group below carries a public api file of its own. That member is
marked `[barrel]` and is the folder the group collapses onto. The failure this design exists
to avoid, two or more merged names each carrying a public api file, occurs in none of the 23
on any of the eight projects: it would silence a genuine cross slice report, and it would be
a reason to stop the release rather than a line in this file.

## How this was measured

Eight public FSD projects, pinned to fixed commits, resolved file by file with the release's
own resolver. The report movement quoted below was taken from real ESLint runs over the same
eight, with the plugin built at the 2.1.0 branch point and at the release. The eight are
`buggregator-frontend`, `cloudhood`, `moonlogs`, `nukeapp`, `polka`, `vkui-audiopad`,
`workout-cool` and `yeahub-platform`.

## Calibration: most of these change nothing you can see

A merged group is not the same thing as a lost report. A group only costs you a report when
something actually imports across two of the merged names, and most of them have nothing
crossing. Of the 23 groups, **5 move a report and the other 18 move none**: `sortable-list`
in `cloudhood`, `album-list` and `track-list` in `vkui-audiopad`, `workout-builder` in
`workout-cool` and `SubscriptionsList` in `yeahub-platform`, which between them account for
the 14 disappearing reports that this class contributes.

## The 23 groups

### buggregator-frontend: 0

None. Every inner folder of this project carries its own public api file, so the deepest
candidate is the folder the old heuristic already picked.

### cloudhood: 3

| Collapses onto | Names that merge into it |
| - | - |
| `src/entities/sortable-list` | `sortable-list` [barrel], `components`, `hooks`, `useSortableList.spec.ts`, `utils.spec.ts` |
| `src/widgets/request-cookies` | `request-cookies` [barrel], `RequestCookieRow` |
| `src/widgets/sidebar` | `sidebar` [barrel], `helpers`, `sidebar.spec.ts` |

### moonlogs: 0

None.

### nukeapp: 1

| Collapses onto | Names that merge into it |
| - | - |
| `src/entities/product` | `product` [barrel], `@x` |

### polka: 0

None. This is the project that decided the rule: `features/book` carries a public api file
and so do `features/book/search`, `features/book/toggle-favorite` and
`features/book/toggle-read`. Taking the shallowest candidate would collapse those three
genuine slices into their group folder and delete every report between them. Taking the
deepest leaves all three with the answer they have today.

| `packages/front/src/widgets/track-list` | `track-list` [barrel], `track`, `gallery`, `list` |

## Total

**23 merged groups across the eight projects.** The names in each row are the last path part
of the folder the old heuristic would have called a slice, which is why two rows can both
name `gallery` or `hooks`.

The reports that actually disappear are a separate, smaller count: 16 across the eight
projects, of which 14 come from this class and 2 come from the unrelated segment prefix fix
described in the release notes.
